title: Daemon: process multiple tasks concurrently (max_concurrency enforcement)
description: Daemon currently processes one task at a time (docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md Phase 2). This is the core blocker between current state and any multi-agent scaling mode — needed before container max_concurrency or same-repo concurrency can matter. Wire the daemon's dispatch loop to run N tasks in parallel, respecting a configurable max_concurrency.
design: internal/container/pool.go already enforces max_concurrency for container lifecycle — reuse that limit/pattern in the daemon's task dispatch rather than inventing a second concurrency control.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon dispatch loop runs multiple tasks concurrently up to a configured max_concurrency limit; single-task-at-a-time behavior is gone.
close_reason: Implemented concurrent SQLite and NATS task dispatch using containers.max_concurrency, with default same-repo serialization and race-tested dispatcher coverage.

title: archie-agent: run full task (workflow.Route + workflow.Run) via RPC-backed TaskContext
description: The actual stage-loop move for archie-core-5zh, depending on the TaskConfig payload and TaskContext interface refactor. cmd/archie-agent gains a handler for a new 'run whole task' NATS message (task summary + TaskConfig + repo config, no secrets). On receipt it: builds its own workflow.Registry via skillbuild.BuildRegistry against its mounted worktree (/data/worktree — same pattern the daemon already uses, no registry needs to cross the wire); calls workflow.Route itself; builds a TaskContext using storerpc.Client (Store), forgerpc.Client (Forge), and a hybrid Trees (worktreerpc.Client for Prepare/Push, a local *worktree.Manager with no token for CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines against the bind-mounted dir); calls workflow.Run; reports completion once instead of round-tripping per stage.
acceptance_criteria: When agent.mode=nats and containers are enabled, archie-agent runs an entire task's workflow (all stages) per invocation, not one stage per round trip; inprocess/subprocess modes are unaffected.
close_reason: Added internal/taskrun (Request/Response wire types + SubjectForTask) and cmd/archie-agent/taskrun.go: runTask builds a workflow.Registry from the container's own bind-mounted worktree (skillbuild.BuildRegistry, same call the daemon already makes), routes and runs the task's entire workflow via workflow.Route/workflow.Run, using storerpc.Client/forgerpc.Client for Store/Forge and a new hybridTrees (worktreerpc.Client for Prepare/Push, local *worktree.Manager for CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines against the mount). Added config.TaskConfig.ToConfig() to rebuild a usable config.Config from the curated payload. Added storage.WorktreeMountDir constant (/data/worktree) — critical fix: hybridTrees.Prepare discards the RPC response's host-side directory and returns the container's fixed local mount path instead, since archied and archie-agent see the same files at different paths. Wired a queue-grouped core-NATS subscription on archie.taskrun.> in cmd/archie-agent/main.go so this is reachable in the running binary, not just testable in isolation. End-to-end test drives the real 'bootstrap' workflow (no LLM) through real storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc servers and a real local git remote, proving the full chain: registry build, route, prepare, commit, push, PR creation, and that the authoritative task state lands in archied's store via RPC. archie-core-5zh.8 (daemon.go handoff) is now unblocked — it owns deciding exactly how/when archied publishes to archie.taskrun.<id>.

title: daemon.go: hand off whole task to archie-agent in sandboxed NATS+container mode
description: Depends on the archie-agent full-task handler existing. internal/daemon/daemon.go's process() currently always calls workflow.Route/workflow.Run itself, dispatching per-stage LLM calls to d.Agent (NATSRunner does this over NATS today). When d.Nats != nil && d.ContainerPool != nil (the sandboxed path this whole PRD phase targets), process() should instead publish one 'run whole task' message to archie-agent and await its completion report, skipping local workflow.Route/workflow.Run entirely. inprocess/subprocess modes (no container pool) keep calling workflow.Run in the daemon exactly as today — this only changes behavior for the fully-sandboxed path.
acceptance_criteria: With containers enabled, daemon.process() delegates the entire task to archie-agent in one round trip; without containers, behavior is unchanged (verified by existing daemon tests continuing to pass).
close_reason: daemon.process() now branches on d.ContainerPool != nil: sandboxed tasks get handed to archie-agent via a new runViaAgent method (publishes taskrun.Request to archie.taskrun.<id>, awaits taskrun.Response) instead of calling workflow.Route/workflow.Run locally; non-container mode is unchanged. runViaAgent only parks the task itself on transport/setup failure (encode error, no responder, decode error, or an error returned before archie-agent's workflow.Run got to run) — on success, every durable side effect already landed via the storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc proxies during archie-agent's run, so runViaAgent just logs. Added agentexec.ProvidersFromConfig (deduped from cmd/archied's former executionProviders). Also fixed a real correctness gap this surfaced: with concurrent multi-task dispatch (u64/g1l) plus containerized archie-agent, the 5zh.7 wildcard queue-group subscription could let one container answer a sibling's taskrun message despite having a different task's worktree mounted. archie-agent now reads its boot-time task.json (container.TaskPayload, already written by daemon.process() before container acquire) and subscribes to its own exact archie.taskrun.<id> subject when present, falling back to the shared queue group only when no task.json exists (dev/pool mode). Full container-mode integration (real Docker) isn't covered by an automated test, consistent with the rest of the container-dependent code — runViaAgent itself is unit-tested directly against embedded NATS, bypassing the Docker-dependent Acquire path. This closes the archie-core-5zh epic: archie-agent now runs an entire task's workflow per invocation instead of one stage per round trip, with Store/Forge/git-push credentials staying daemon-side throughout.

title: Register storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc servers in archied startup
description: Depends on the TaskContext interface refactor. cmd/archied/main.go builds the Daemon with Store/Forge/Trees but never registers the storerpc.Server/forgerpc.Server/worktreerpc.Server handlers, so archie-agent's RPC calls currently have no responder in production. Wire all three Register(nc) calls into archied's startup when cfg.NATS is configured, alongside the existing NATS client connect.
acceptance_criteria: When [nats] is configured, archied subscribes to all storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc subjects at startup; an archie-agent container can successfully call Store/Forge/worktree operations against a running archied.
close_reason: Added registerTaskRPCServers() in cmd/archied/main.go, wiring storerpc.Server/forgerpc.Server/worktreerpc.Server onto the daemon's NATS connection whenever [nats] is configured, alongside the existing worktree.Manager and forge/store instances the daemon already owns. Test spins an embedded NATS server, registers via the composed function, then round-trips real storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc clients against it to prove all three are reachable. archie-core-5zh.7 (archie-agent full-task handler) can now be built and tested end-to-end against a real archied.

title: Curated TaskConfig payload for archie-agent (no secrets)
description: Groundwork for archie-core-5zh.4. workflow.TaskContext.Cfg (config.Config) is read throughout stages (Models, Budgets, Dispatch incl. label mapping, DiffCapLines, Notify.Webhook, Forge.Host) but the full Config also carries forge/NATS credentials that must never enter the agent container. Add a config.TaskConfig struct — same field names/shapes as the subset config.Config exposes (Models, Budgets, Dispatch, DiffCapLines, Notify, Forge) — with json tags, plus a constructor (e.g. config.Config.ForTask()) that builds it from the daemon's live config. Add json tags to config.Repo's remaining fields (only AllowConcurrent has them today) since tc.Repo also needs to cross the wire.
acceptance_criteria: config.TaskConfig marshals/unmarshals via JSON and carries exactly the fields workflow stages read; no token/credential field is reachable from it; config.Repo fully round-trips through JSON.
close_reason: Implemented curated non-secret TaskConfig/TaskForge payload with detached map snapshots, stable JSON Duration encoding, full Repo JSON tags, and regression coverage. Focused config tests, go vet, go fix -diff, and full race suite pass; repository-wide lint remains blocked only by 36 unrelated pre-existing findings.

title: TaskContext interface refactor: Forge/Store/Trees as trimmed interfaces
description: Groundwork for archie-core-5zh.4. workflow.TaskContext currently types Forge/Store/Trees as concrete daemon types (forge.Forge interface already, *store.Store, *worktree.Manager). Define trimmed interfaces in internal/workflow scoped to exactly the methods stages call (Forge: Comment/CloseIssue/CreatePR/SetStateLabel; Store: Update/Transition; Trees: Prepare/CommitAll/Push/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines) so storerpc.Client, forgerpc.Client, and a worktreerpc-backed implementation can satisfy them from inside archie-agent, while *store.Store/*worktree.Manager and the real forge.Forge implementations keep satisfying them unchanged for the daemon's existing inprocess/subprocess paths.
acceptance_criteria: TaskContext.Forge/Store/Trees are interface-typed; daemon.go compiles and all existing tests pass unchanged (concrete types satisfy the new interfaces structurally); no behavior change for inprocess/subprocess modes.
close_reason: Trimmed workflow.TaskContext.Forge/Store/Trees to new interfaces (Forger, TaskStore, Trees) in internal/workflow/workflow.go, scoped to exactly the methods stages call mid-run (4 Forge methods, 2 Store methods, 6 Trees methods). Go's structural typing meant zero changes were needed anywhere else — forge.Forge (already an interface), *store.Store, and *worktree.Manager all satisfy the new interfaces automatically, and storerpc.Client/forgerpc.Client/worktreerpc.Client already match by construction from 5zh.1-3. Full build, race suite, vet, and staticcheck all clean with no behavior change. archie-core-5zh.7 (archie-agent full-task handler) and 5zh.9 (register RPC servers in archied) are now unblocked.

title: Forge RPC proxy: archie-agent → archied for forge API calls
description: Phase 1 groundwork for archie-core-5zh. Stages call Forge.SetStateLabel/Comment/CreatePR/CloseIssue/CreateIssue/React/RepliesAfter mid-workflow. Forge holds live API tokens (Gitea/GitHub) that must stay daemon-side per the PRD's 'daemon never runs untrusted code, owns all secrets' boundary. Once workflow.Run moves into archie-agent, these calls need to become NATS request/reply RPCs to the daemon rather than shipping forge credentials into the agent container.
acceptance_criteria: archie-agent can invoke the forge.Forge interface methods used by workflow stages over NATS; archied executes them against the real forge client and replies; no forge API tokens are present in the agent container.
close_reason: Added internal/forgerpc: core-NATS request/reply RPC for the four forge.Forge methods workflow stages actually call mid-run (Comment, CloseIssue, CreatePR, SetStateLabel). Confirmed via grep that all other Forge methods (AssignedIssues, IssuesWithLabel, React, RepliesAfter, PRState, CreateIssue, AcceptInvitations, VerifyPush) are daemon-only poll/reconcile-loop calls, never invoked from a workflow stage, so nothing else needs proxying. archied stays the sole holder of forge API tokens. Not yet wired into daemon.go or workflow.TaskContext — deferred to archie-core-5zh.4.

title: Worktree push RPC proxy: archie-agent → archied for git push
description: Phase 1 groundwork for archie-core-5zh. worktree.Manager.Push needs the forge HTTPS push token (held daemon-side, used via an askpass helper). Trees.Prepare/CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines are local git operations against the already-mounted worktree and can run agent-side unchanged (containers already bind-mount /data/worktree) — only Push needs to be proxied back to the daemon, which holds the credential.
acceptance_criteria: archie-agent can request a git push over NATS; archied performs the authenticated push using its held token and replies with success/failure; the push token is never sent to or stored in the agent container.
close_reason: Added internal/worktreerpc: core-NATS request/reply RPC so archie-agent can request a git push without holding the forge push token. Server resolves the worktree directory itself from owner/repo/issue (never trusts a path from the sandboxed agent) and calls the daemon's own worktree.Manager.Push, which already holds the token via its askpass helper. Prepare/CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines stay local git ops the agent can run directly against its bind-mounted worktree — only Push needed proxying. Not yet wired into daemon.go or workflow.TaskContext — deferred to archie-core-5zh.4, which now has all three RPC proxies (Store, Forge, worktree push) it depends on.

title: Move workflow.Route/workflow.Run stage loop into archie-agent
description: Final step of archie-core-5zh, depends on the Store/Forge/push RPC proxies existing. Move workflow.Route + workflow.Run's stage-loop execution from internal/daemon/daemon.go's process() into cmd/archie-agent, using the RPC proxies for Store/Forge/push and reimplementing CustomStages discovery (wfeval.Discover) agent-side against the already-mounted worktree. daemon.process() keeps worktree prepare + container acquire/release, then hands off the whole task to archie-agent in one NATS round trip instead of one round trip per stage.
acceptance_criteria: workflow.Route and workflow.Run execute inside archie-agent, not archied, when agent.mode=nats; archie-agent handles a full task (not a single stage) per invocation; inprocess/subprocess modes keep working unchanged.
close_reason: Superseded by finer-grained sub-issues 5zh.5 (TaskConfig payload), 5zh.6 (TaskContext interface refactor), 5zh.7 (archie-agent full-task handler), 5zh.8 (daemon.go handoff), 5zh.9 (register RPC servers in archied). The original single acceptance criterion (workflow.Route/Run execute in archie-agent) is satisfied once 5zh.7 and 5zh.8 land; splitting further because implementation revealed real design forks (Prepare needing the push token, tc.Cfg needing a curated non-secret payload) that each warrant their own test-first pass.

title: Store RPC proxy: archie-agent → archied for task state mutations
description: Phase 1 groundwork for archie-core-5zh. workflow.Run calls tc.Store.Update every stage and tc.Store.Transition on terminal outcomes — Store wraps a direct SQLite *sql.DB handle that only the daemon owns. Once workflow.Run moves into archie-agent, these calls need to become NATS request/reply RPCs to the daemon (the sole DB owner), reusing the existing AgentRequestMessage/reply-inbox plumbing pattern (internal/agentexec/nats.go) rather than giving the agent container direct DB access.
acceptance_criteria: archie-agent can call Store.Update and Store.Transition equivalents over NATS; archied executes them against SQLite and replies; no direct DB access from the agent container.
close_reason: Added internal/storerpc: core-NATS request/reply RPC so archie-agent can call Store.Update/Transition without direct DB access. archied's Store stays the sole owner; store.Task gained json tags to cross the wire. Not yet wired into daemon.go or workflow.TaskContext — that's archie-core-5zh.4's job once all three RPC proxies exist.

title: ContainerRunner: implement agentexec.Runner against Docker for sandboxed execution
description: Phase 2 of docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md. agentexec.Runner (InProcessRunner/SubprocessRunner) is an interface deliberately designed to be swapped for a container-backed runner without touching workflow orchestration. internal/container/pool.go already handles Docker lifecycle (pull, create, start, release, orphan recovery). Implement ContainerRunner against the existing Runner interface.
design: Do not redesign the execution boundary — implement strictly against the existing Runner interface per its doc comments.
acceptance_criteria: ContainerRunner implements agentexec.Runner, runs tasks in ephemeral Docker containers with workspace bind-mounted, and is selectable via [agent] mode = "nats" + containers.enabled = true.

title: Promote archie-agent to per-task process; move workflow routing out of archied
description: cmd/archie-agent exists but only executes one workflow stage per invocation over the internal/agentexec stdin/stdout JSON protocol (v1). Phase 1 of the PRD requires promoting it to the PRD's per-task process model, moving workflow.Route/workflow.Run out of archied and into archie-agent.
acceptance_criteria: workflow.Route and workflow.Run execute inside archie-agent, not archied; archie-agent handles a full task (not a single stage) per invocation.

title: NATS transport: JetStream task queue + request-reply between daemon and archie-agent
description: Phase 1 of docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md. internal/events.Bus (in-process pub/sub, already feeding SQLite + SSE) is the natural seam to replace the transport under. Daemon publishes tasks, archie-agent consumes, results return via NATS. Preserve current inprocess mode via [agent] mode default for local dev.
design: Add optional [nats] config block (url, token_env), default anonymous auth for single-node, credentials required for multi-node per PRD sec.9 open question 2.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon can dispatch a task to archie-agent over NATS JetStream and receive results via request-reply; inprocess mode still works unchanged.
close_reason: Completed JetStream task dispatch and NATS agent request/reply, including token_env authentication for archied and canonical NATS_URL/NATS_TOKEN propagation to container workers; anonymous local mode remains supported and race-tested.

title: Audit archie-core repo for bugs/improvements, file as Gitea issues
description: Fan out exploration subagents across internal/ subsystems to find bugs, tech debt, and enhancement opportunities. Each confirmed finding gets filed as a Gitea issue on git.catlow.cloud/sam/archie-core.
close_reason: Audit complete: 58 Gitea issues (#3-#60) filed at git.catlow.cloud/sam/archie-core. 60 raw findings, 59 verified, 58 successfully filed. 8 agents hit session limit at end (webui/workflow/worktree file-phase).

title: Per-repo allow_concurrent override for same-repo multi-agent work
description: Concurrent agents on the same repo are blocked by default (worktree conflict). PRD sec.9 open question 5 proposes a per-repo config override (allow_concurrent = true) for repos where parallel work is safe (different base branches, different packages). Deferred to Phase 2 in the PRD; depends on the daemon supporting concurrent task dispatch at all.
acceptance_criteria: Repos with allow_concurrent = true in [[repos]] config can have multiple agents working simultaneously without worktree collisions; repos without it keep current serialized behavior.
close_reason: Added config.Repo.AllowConcurrent (allow_concurrent toml key) and threaded it through taskDispatcher so opted-in repos skip the default FIFO same-repo serialization while still respecting containers.max_concurrency. Worktrees are already keyed per issue number, so no on-disk collision. Race-tested dispatcher coverage added.

title: Persistent volumes with TTL for container/worktree storage
description: Phase 2 of docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md. Current worktree lifecycle is fresh-clone-per-task with status-driven cleanup, no TTL. Add persistent volume support with TTL-based expiry to avoid repeated full clones for repeated work on the same repo.
acceptance_criteria: Container/worktree storage can persist across tasks for the same repo up to a configured TTL, with automatic cleanup after expiry.
